summary: The token meter in src/core/tokens is a pure counter that learns each model from usage its replies report. The scene turn loop supplies committed reply usage, while tool-round requests are skipped because their usage covers more than one request. A gpt-tokenizer base count is calibrated against reported prompt totals, including cache usage, with a display midpoint and an upper budgeting bound. Usage readers avoid invented zeros, cache planning predicts cost, and history trimming preserves cache-friendly boundaries. Learned StateStore data contains numbers rather than prompt content. Prompt-block text files become literal user messages and participate in text counting. Image and PDF bytes are never tokenized as base64 prose; their model-specific costs are locally unknown. Inspector, forecast and recorded-request views label those estimates incomplete, and a text budget passing does not guarantee multimodal context fit. Independent file-count and byte ceilings still apply, and providers can enforce smaller model or request limits. The page also documents calibration, uncertainty, cache behavior and the deterministic source tests supporting those algorithms.

sections.title: Attached files
sections.summary: Text-file attachments enter the same request text counter as other literal messages. The meter does not count base64 payloads as prose or invent image/PDF token prices. When native media is present, Inspector, forecast and recorded-request views expose an incomplete-estimate notice. Consequently, a request passing the text budget can still exceed a provider's complete multimodal context. The independent byte and file-count ceilings remain active, and the selected provider or model can reject input under smaller limits. This boundary distinguishes a useful text estimate from a guarantee about total media cost.

sections.title: Why it learns
sections.summary: No local tokenizer is exact for most models: Anthropic's current tokenizer has no open-source build, Gemini counts exactly only over the network, and each open-weight family has its own vocabulary. Every reply reports what its whole prompt cost, though. So the meter counts each prompt one cheap, consistent way and learns per model how that count maps onto the reported one, getting closer the more you generate, for any model on any provider.

sections.title: The pieces
sections.summary: The base counter runs o200k on each message's exact text, split into prose, code, JSON and CJK, treats special-token text as text, and adds 4 tokens of framing per message. countText, the raw total, owns one bounded content-hash cache every caller shares (lore, prompt trace, editor badges), so unchanged text is never re-encoded; countMessage layers its own exact-text LRU on top for the class split. The usage reader maps every major provider shape into one record whose total counts cached tokens once. The fits use recursive least squares from a family prior, with a bound for report wander and fit uncertainty. A cached slice is learned as a second measurement. Reports under half the base are refused, early high reports wait for repeats, and a tokenizer change is re-learned. The meter document holds numbers only. Both token caches empty when the library locks, and a gate keeps them from being read or filled while it stays locked, so a turn that finishes after a lock never caches decrypted text.

sections.title: What is tested
sections.summary: Usage fixtures are built from provider documentation and say so. Synthetic models with a known tokenizer and seeded noise, across 200 seeds, prove the bound covers the truth on at least 97 percent of fresh prompts from zero replies on, including models above their prior, small prompts, normal noise, many short messages, and noisier models checked seed by seed. The bound never overcounts past a sendable multiple of its midpoint. Cached parts, breakpoint or automatic, with hits on older entries, never push a bound under the truth. Each smaller rule has its own test.
